questions.solution:

\begin{aligned}

& =\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{~b}^2}{2 \mathrm{ac}}\right)-1=\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}{2 \mathrm{ac}}\right)-1=\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}{2 \mathrm{ac}}+1\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}{2 \mathrm{ac}}-1\right) \\
& =\frac{(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c})^2(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{c})^2}{(2 \mathrm{ac})^2} \\
& =\left[\frac{(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c})(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{c})}{2 \mathrm{ac}}\right]=\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^2-\mathrm{c}^2}{2 \mathrm{ac}}\right)^2

Force on each conductor is given by

questions.solution:
The weight of the disc is balanced by the force due to the surface tension and the upthrust of water.
The component of surface tension in vertically upward direction is $\mathrm{T} \cos \theta$ and the force acting due to it $2 \pi \mathrm{r} \mathrm{T} \cos \theta$.
The upthrust is equal to the weight of the water displaced (W).
$\therefore$ Weight of the disc $=2 \pi \mathrm{rT} \cos \theta+\mathrm{W}$
